To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) predictive monitoring techniques are applicable for a wide range of lead-times and (b) the combination of predictive monitoring techniques can improve prediction accuracy.

the accuracy of the prediction process is highly dependent on the point in process execution when the prediction is made and the lead-time for accurate predictions, and that the combination of different prediction techniques may improve the prediction process with respect to certain accuracy indicators.
(1) the three predictive monitoring techniques differ with regard to their accuracy and (2) the combination of the three techniques can improve the accuracy of predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to reliably and accurately predict potential process problems in advance and how to exploit the characteristics of different techniques to improve the prediction process.
the applicability of predictive monitoring in general and the combination of existing prediction techniques in particular.
the applicability, accuracy, and combination of predictive business process monitoring techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single predictive monitoring technique is superior to the other ones.
all techniques have their strengths and weaknesses and that the best approach depends on the specific use case and accuracy indicators.

the combination of constraint satisfaction with QQS aggregation provides the best results in terms of recall and precision, and that the combination of machine learning with constraint satisfiability provides the best results for F-measure and accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, given an appropriate lead-time, predictive monitoring techniques are applicable in practice, but that the selection of the most appropriate technique depends on the specific accuracy indicators that are to be improved.

the accuracy of the individual techniques is not only dependent on the lead-time of the prediction but also on the specific prediction problem at hand, i.e., whether the prediction is about a potential violation or nonviolation.
, in general, the techniques are complementary and should be used together to achieve the best possible accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the applicability of predictive monitoring techniques is not limited to the detection of potential problems.
, in order to improve the prediction process in business process monitoring, the individual characteristics of the prediction techniques need to be considered.
the combination of predictive monitoring techniques is a promising approach for increasing the accuracy of predictions.
